facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's policy states that the national HMIS is paper at the facility level, in registers and monthly return forms, and electronic at the regional health directorates and the central level, in the DHIS2 database; the policy gives no date for this, so its published date is used.

The policy places the electronic HMIS at the seven regional health directorates and the Ministry only, with facilities reporting on paper registers and monthly return forms; no facility tier is said to use DHIS2. Undated in the policy, so its published date is used.

The policy states that the HMIS at the facility level is paper registers and monthly return forms, with electronic entry only at regional health directorates and centrally; it gives no count of facilities and no date, so its published date is used.

The policy calls DHIS2 the national electronic system used at the Ministry of Health to manage health information and the central reporting system for all national health information, with the HMIS programme under the Directorate of Planning and Information; undated, so the published date is used.

The National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030 names the HMIS and DHIS2, sets the strategy of migrating fully from paper recording to a computerised system with internet at all levels, and lists a costed National Health Sector Strategic Plan 2021-2025 as its implementing document; the published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's policy states that the health sector does not have a robust electronic medical record system in place and that sufficient ICT infrastructure is needed to establish one; it names no facility using one. Undated, so the published date is used.

The policy states the sector has no robust electronic medical record system and sets the strategy of migrating fully from paper-based recording to a computerised system at all levels of care; undated, so the published date is used.

The National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030 has a section on the Electronic Medical Record System, stating the need to establish and implement it across all levels and for the Ministry to integrate existing databases into one system; no budget or timetable is given, and the published date is used.
